# Environment flag reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/flag-reference.mjs. Every column except Description is
regenerated from the sources; Description is merged by key, so hand edits
survive regeneration. Regenerate with: node scripts/flag-reference.mjs
CI runs --check and fails when a key the code reads has no row here, or a row
names a key nothing reads. -->

A flag is an environment key the code reads. This table is the generated
inventory of every one the scanner can see in `src/**/*.ts`,
`web/src/**/*.ts(x)` and `scripts/*.mjs` (tests and fixtures excluded);
[DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md) remains the prose authority for the model behind the
settings that matter and for where each flag must be set. Columns:

- **Default** — the literal in the read's own fallback (`??`, `||`, or a
  ternary), when there is one; anything else says "see source".
- **Accepted** — the value grammar the reading code accepts, when it is
  derivable (a known helper, or the comparisons on the read's own line).
  Ship's boolean grammars differ by flag; this column never guesses.
- **Read at** — the first three `file:line` sites.
- **Side** — web, worker or both, by file location (`web/src` = web). The web
  process also runs the ship package's enqueue paths, so a "worker" key can be
  read by both processes; the Description column says where to SET a flag.
- **Description** — hand-maintained. "TODO" means nobody has written it yet.

Rows named like `SHIP_EVENT_SECRET_<...>` are read patterns: the code reads
every key with that prefix, built at runtime.

| `SHIP_DELEGATE` | see source | 0/false/no/off (flag defaults on) | src/runtime.ts:1401 | worker | Offer the ```delegate action (S20/S22, bounded child work): the agent spawns ONE child run — a READ-ONLY SCAN run carrying its lineage (`parentRunId`, the task root) and its gates (trust, network tier, spend source, all copied from the parent's recorded input, never widened; nothing change-shaped is copied) — then parks until the child finishes and merges its summary back as its next observation, a recorded CONTEXT TRANSFER on the `turn-N-delegate-wait` step. Since the 2026-10-17 live finding, children NEVER edit, push or open pull requests (scan mode: publish gate disabled, ```edit/```create refused), never park on a human decision (asks not offered and refused by name; approval-required actions denied automatically with the reason recorded), and the parent remains the only writer producing the single PR — the child's deliverable is the findings/answer/proposed-patch report in its summary. Off by default and byte-identical when off: the action is not parseable and the prompt does not mention it. The park reuses the ask machinery's snapshot/restore over the engine's sleeping-run wake (the worker already wakes sleeping runs), so no new sweep or wake source exists; a parked parent releases its slot and repo lock, and the child rides the ordinary admission. Children are marked `delegateChild` and can never themselves delegate (refused by name), and the flag never reaches them even with this set. Materialised into the run input at enqueue (it admits the `turn-N-delegate-*` steps), so only newly-enqueued runs get it and replays return the recorded transfer without touching the child. Suppressed on scans. See `docs/COORDINATOR_DESIGN.md`. |
| `SHIP_DELEGATE_MAX` | "" | see source | src/delegate.ts:47 | worker | Hard cap on delegated children per TASK ROOT, counted from the root's delegation ledger (a config-store record; same-process claims serialise under the file lock, cross-process the deterministic child id plus the launch journal is the boundary). Refusals reach the model as an observation, never a failed run. Clamped to at most 16; junk values fall back to the default. |
| `SHIP_DELEGATE_TARGETS` | see source | see source | src/delegate-targets.ts:192, src/runtime.ts:2124 | worker | Where a delegated child may run (DT2): an allowlist of targets the parent names with ```delegate target=<id>. JSON `[{"id":"glm","harness":"native","model":"zai/glm-5.3"}]` (or `{"glm":{"harness":…,"model":…}}`), or the simple list `glm=native:zai/glm-5.3,cc=claude-code:glm-5.3`. Ids are lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; harnesses must be known; a malformed value allows nothing. A project narrows it with `teploy-ship project set <repo> --delegate-targets <id,id>\|none` (`""` clears back to the whole list). Every targeted spawn runs the routing policy's data-class gate (destination, then retention, then the rest of `whyNot`) **whatever `SHIP_MODEL_ROUTING` is set to**: with no `SHIP_MODEL_ROUTING_POLICY` loaded, every target is refused; a model the policy does not list is refused; the task facts are `SHIP_MODEL_ROUTING_DATA_CLASS` / `_DESTINATIONS` / `_MAX_RETENTION` (default `private`, nothing allowed). An external-harness target must name the model this deployment configures for that harness (`SHIP_HARNESS_MODEL[_<ID>]`), and the provider host its forwarded env selects must equal the policy entry's destination host. Each refusal reaches the parent as an observation naming its code. An admitted child records `delegateTarget` (target, policy version, file digest, destination) in its input, executes on the target's model (`input.model`) and is priced on it, and gets a `selection` row in `ship_model_segments`. Offered targets are materialised into the parent's input at enqueue (`delegateTargets`, only with `SHIP_DELEGATE` on), so set it on both web and worker; a delegation without `target=` is unchanged. |

| `SHIP_FORK` | "" | 0/false/no/off | src/fork.ts:35 | worker | `on` offers **Fork run** on a settled run's page (DF1, `src/fork.ts`): a fork is a NEW task that carries the source's recorded history as text (the D3 prior-run context, materialised into its task at enqueue), starts a new `ship/<forkRunId>` branch at the source's last recorded pushed commit — or the default branch when it pushed nothing, which the task says — and opens a pull request of its own; the source run's PR and branch are untouched (that is the difference from a follow-up, which edits the same PR). Only `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled` runs, or one parked at its merge review, may be forked; anything else in flight is refused by name (`FORK_SOURCE_NOT_SETTLED`, naming the run and its state) inside the enqueue, so every surface — page, HTTP API (`fork` in `examples/http-client.mjs`), a future CLI — gets the same refusal and a stale tab cannot fork a resumed run. Authority is the follow-up's (`approve`: editor or above, actor recorded). Lineage is recorded as `input.forkOf` — never `parentRunId`, because a fork is its own task root — and shown on the run page and in the thread view. Admits NO workflow step, so runs without it replay byte-identically and a fork shares the fingerprint of the equivalent non-fork run; set it on BOTH web and worker (the web container enqueues the fork). |

One knob rather than three because the three are only safe together: an sslip.io hostname without the allowlist is a public, unauthenticated HTTP preview. Unset, the argv is exactly what it was before (no version call). **Set it on the web process too:** the dashboard's CSP frames exactly `http://*.<ip>.sslip.io` and nothing else, and the run page's preview panel frames the preview's own hostname (never a dashboard path); without it on the web process the panel offers the open-in-tab link and says why there is no frame. `smoke`, `visual-diff` and `flow` run in the **sandbox**, behind its allowlist proxy, so for a project that declares a preview Ship adds `.<ip>.sslip.io` (every preview on this target — a leading-dot suffix is the narrowest form the daemon's grammar has) plus main's host when the visual rung is declared and `SHIP_PREVIEW_MAIN_URL` names one, to the run's sandbox allowlist at enqueue, after the project's own entries (which always survive). No per-project `--egress-allow` entry is needed. Resolved from the ENQUEUEING process's env (web and worker both carry it; an operator-shell `teploy-ship enqueue` without it records only the project's entries). The allowlist proxy dials from the sandbox host, so the preview target sees that host's tailnet address. A follow-up on an existing pull request removes the previews of that pull request's older runs once its own preview is up (`preview-supersede` step): previews stay per revision, and a run never removes the preview of a run enqueued after it. |

Only the exact value `on` enables it; anything else is off, and off is a strict no-op (no store read, no forge call). Watches every PR a run OPENED (a recorded `repo-pr` step; the forge head must be `ship/…`) — but only PRs opened within `SHIP_PR_WATCH_MAX_AGE_DAYS` days, and the first enable starts its discovery cursor at that window instead of walking all history — and polls it with forge API reads only — never a model call — so idle watched PRs cost nothing but a few HTTP reads. A merge conflict (`mergeable=false`) or a failing check on the head SHA proposes exactly ONE revision task on the same PR through the ordinary intake path, so source/project policy, budgets and auto windows decide whether it waits in the Inbox or launches: conflicts use source `pr-watch`, failing checks source `ci` with the CI webhook's own dedupe key (`ci:<owner/repo>#<pr>:<sha>`), so a `workflow_run` delivery and a poll of the same head collapse to one task. Dedupe = PR + head SHA + reason; a dismissed task is not re-proposed for the same head; a new head is eligible again. Conflict wins when both hold. Failing check = `failure`/`error`/`timed_out`/`action_required`; when the base branch's protection is readable and names required contexts, only those count, otherwise every failing check does. Merged, closed or 30-day-old watches are dropped. State is small `SHIP_PR_WATCH_*` rows in the runtime config store — no new table. Forges without webhooks (and external CI that reports commit statuses) are covered by the polling alone. |

Accepts only `on` (`1`/`true` leave it off — the `SHIP_THREAD_VIEW` grammar). With it: the agent may write a ```reply block before its action — a message into the operator's thread that does not end the turn or pause the run (read off the recorded think text, no step of its own); each operator message carries a mode — `steer` (default, today's behaviour: applied at the next turn boundary) or `queue` (held until the agent's next checkpoint: the turn after it posts a reply, or its next ```finish, which the message then holds); and an operator **interrupt** stops the in-flight action at its next safe point — before it starts (effect recorded `not done`), or, for a python kernel cell, by a real cancel (effect `unknown`). A running bash command or edit **cannot** be cancelled (the executor contract has no abort): it runs to completion, is recorded `done`, and the interrupt is delivered right after. The run page's steer composer gains a steer/queue toggle and an interrupt button on such runs; queue and interrupt are refused for runs enqueued without the flag; the thread view (`SHIP_THREAD_VIEW`) shows agent replies, modes and interrupt effects. Off by default and byte-identical when off: prompt, parse and step sequence unchanged. Materialised into the run input at enqueue (`steerReply`; it admits the `turn-N-held` / `turn-N-finish-held` steps), so set it on BOTH web and worker (the web container enqueues UI tasks) and only newly-enqueued runs get it. Queued messages and interrupts live in their own lazily-created table (`ship_steer_held`); plain notes stay in `ship_steer`. See `docs/STEERING_DESIGN.md`. |
